The three policy attributes were shown first or last (trial_order); order within blocks randomized but not recorded. 3,698 respondents = the article's valid N after its filter (IP in country, consent, citizen, resident, 18+, finished). Questionnaire codes for covariates differ by country.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = preferred neighbourhood budget of two (forced choice; verbatim wording not published); rating = approval of each budget, 1 completely disapprove to 7 completely approve. Only 4 of 5 randomized attributes: the winning project shown is not in the deposit (the authors' derived favorability, respondent rating of that project > 4, is dropped). Levels are the authors' English labels. Attribute order randomized, not recorded. cov_ codes unlabelled except as noted in the script; cov_pref_* = respondent's 1-7 preference for each project type.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). No choice question; five 0-100 ratings per profile: rating_impolite (polite-impolite), rating_unacceptable (acceptable-unacceptable), rating_notnormal (normal-not normal), rating_wrong (right-wrong), all kept as asked (higher = more uncivil), and rating = feeling thermometer toward the candidate (cold/unfavourable 0 - warm/favourable 100). Exact item wording not deposited (report paraphrase). Restrictions not documented. 70 respondents with no ratings or unsaved attributes omitted; cov_in_authors_sample marks the authors' 1,884 (attention, straight-lining, speed), of whom 1,843 are in the table.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which of these politicians would you rather have as your Representative in Congress?", forced choice between two text profiles, no opt-out. Restricted randomization: some professions require higher education (Doctor, Lawyer, Teacher about half as frequent). cov_survey_weight is the YouGov weight; the same 500 respondents also answered the visual version (vecchiato_2025_candidates_visual). The article says 5 tasks per respondent; the data have 10.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which of these politicians would you rather have as your Representative in Congress?", forced choice between two mock Twitter profiles, no opt-out; 8 skipped tasks omitted. Attribute levels are the authors' labels decoded from the image file names (race shown only in the photo, feedback as follower/like counts, religion 'No Religion' = none in the bio); the two partisan tweet variants per profile are not stored. Restricted randomization (professions by education). The authors' own processed file codes profession differently for 919 profiles; this table follows the images.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two activist profiles made the respondent feel more represented (forced, no opt-out); rating = how represented the respondent felt by each profile, 1-7, higher = more represented (article wording paraphrased; the article calls it both 7-point and six-point, data run 1-7). Attribute values are the authors' codes for photo/name and tweet manipulations, not displayed text. Respondents got one of 100 pre-drawn design versions; pooled level shares are uniform but shares within a task/profile slot are unequal and attributes are not independent. Germany, Italy, Romania and Sweden pooled (cov_country); N = 8,279 as in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One profile per task: respondents rated each hypothetical immigrant by the likelihood of belonging to an "illegal/undocumented immigrant" group, 0 = Extremely unlikely to 10 = Extremely likely (higher = judged more likely undocumented). No choice question. Levels independently randomized, but police record and government benefits are no/yes with probability 1/2 each, the yes half split equally across specific crimes (3) and programmes (4). The article reports 935 respondents (after dropping 79 straight-liners); 7 of them have no conjoint rows in the deposit, so the table has 928.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcomes: forced choice 'Which refugee should receive the visa?' (choice) and 'which refugee would be more likely to integrate successfully after arriving in the United States?' (choice_integrate), no opt-out. The article reports 5,175 profile pairs while the deposit holds 5,585 (1,117 x 5). Unlabelled survey codes and Qualtrics IDs dropped; randomization details not documented.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two presidential candidates the respondent picks (options 'Opción 1', 'Opción 2', 'Ninguno'; question wording not deposited); OPT-OUT: 'Ninguno' chosen in 6,184 of 15,375 tasks, both profiles 0 (the authors drop these). Attributes randomized simultaneously; levels are the authors' English labels of the Spanish display. Age levels are 40/50/60 in the data (the article text says 35/45/55/65). Cell (cov_survey_weight) and rake (cov_weight_rake) post-stratification weights kept; main estimates are unweighted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two income tax plans the respondent prefers (wording not deposited; paraphrase), forced, no opt-out. Profiles give the marginal tax rate in six income brackets and the revenue the plan would raise relative to current revenue; the revenue attribute was shown to 2,000 respondents (the authors' main sample) and not to 250 (attr_revenue '(not shown)', trial_saw_revenue = 0). Survey weight kept.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single-profile design: choice = would the respondent re-elect the politician in the profile (1 yes / 0 no; a no is the outside option, so opt-out yes); rating_competence = competence rating 1 (least) to 10 (most competent); wording not deposited (codebook descriptions). Attribute levels are the authors' English labels; the survey's display language and the selection of these 927 of 1,800 survey respondents are not documented in the deposit. Rows with neither outcome (7) omitted. Licence CC BY-NC 4.0.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = does the respondent prefer this candidate over the paired one; choice_men / choice_women = would men / women in the respondent's community prefer this candidate (codebook wording, paraphrased); each one per task, no documented opt-out, NA on both profiles when unanswered (302, 110, 92 of 3,492 tasks). rating = competence, 1 (least competent) to 10 (most competent). Question order randomized (trial_outcome_order_1/_2). CC BY-NC 4.0.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which of these judges do you trust more to fairly hear this case on <type> discrimination?' (forced, no opt-out); rating_ideology 1-7 (Very liberal to Very conservative), rating_politically_motivated 1-7 (Impartial to Politically motivated), rating_court_trust 1-4 (Not at all to A great deal) for trusting the Supreme Court if the judge joined it. Levels drawn independently and uniformly; attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_); the case's discrimination type is a respondent-level arm (trial_discrim_type). 4,334 respondents answered at least one pair, 4,042 (the authors' sample) all five; tasks not reached are omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Based on this information, which ONE of these two MPs would you prefer to have as your MP in the House of Commons?" (MP 1 / MP 2; a response was required, no opt-out). Attributes completely independently randomized with equal probabilities (article). Level text is the bold part of each bullet (e.g. dissent 'never'..'often' within '<He/She> ... speaks out or votes against his/her party leadership'); profile position is inferred from row order. N = 1,899 as in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Based on this information, which ONE of these two MPs would you prefer to have as your MP?" (the Study 2 question without 'in the House of Commons'; no opt-out). Motivation ('own personal views' / "constituents' views") and dissent type (three levels from 'nevertheless tends not to speak out' to 'tends to speak out at internal party meetings and also publicly') are the article's quoted wording mapped from the authors' labels; profile position is inferred from row order. N = 1,919 as in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Three forced choices per pair (choice = the authors' main outcome outcome_q3; choice_q1, choice_q2 = alternative outcomes); the question wording is not in the deposit, no opt-out. Task and profile are inferred from row order (verified one chosen per pair). Attribute levels are the authors' English translations; the authors' matched subsample is not included.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One vignette per task; choice = 1 if the respondent answered Yes to "should the Chinese government prevent the proposed transaction?" (English version of the Chinese instrument; single-profile yes/no, so opt_out = yes). Four attributes; level text is the authors' short English labels, not the Chinese display text. No restrictions documented. Task order inferred from row order; three ids with 10 rows dropped; 1,613 respondents vs 1,659 recruited.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One vignette per task; choice = 1 if the respondent answered Yes to "should the United States government prevent the proposed transaction?" (0 = No; single-profile yes/no, so opt_out = yes). Six attributes filled into a text template; no restrictions or probabilities documented (authors analyse it as uniform). Task order inferred from row order; one id with 10 rows dropped; 2,003 respondents vs 2,010 recruited.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two hypothetical countries (A/B) the respondent would prefer to be born and grow up in (forced, no opt-out); rating = how happy the respondent would be to have been born and grown up in each country, 1 = extremely unhappy to 7 = extremely happy. Levels independently randomized with equal probability; attribute order randomized per respondent (only the position of the democracy block is recorded). N = 1,008 as in the paper; attribute text as displayed in the survey language.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two hypothetical countries (A/B) the respondent would prefer to be born and grow up in (forced, no opt-out); rating = how happy the respondent would be to have been born and grown up in each country, 1 = extremely unhappy to 7 = extremely happy. Levels independently randomized with equal probability; attribute order randomized per respondent (only the position of the democracy block is recorded). N = 1,022 as in the paper; attribute text as displayed in the survey language. Respondents chose Hindi or English (cov_survey_language) but the export stores the attribute text in Hindi only; one respondent-wealth level has two Unicode spellings (as stored; the authors merge them).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two hypothetical countries (A/B) the respondent would prefer to be born and grow up in (forced, no opt-out); rating = how happy the respondent would be to have been born and grown up in each country, 1 = extremely unhappy to 7 = extremely happy. Levels independently randomized with equal probability; attribute order randomized per respondent (only the position of the democracy block is recorded). N = 1,047 as in the paper; attribute text as displayed in the survey language.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two hypothetical countries (A/B) the respondent would prefer to be born and grow up in (forced, no opt-out); rating = how happy the respondent would be to have been born and grown up in each country, 1 = extremely unhappy to 7 = extremely happy. Levels independently randomized with equal probability; attribute order randomized per respondent (only the position of the democracy block is recorded). N = 1,012 as in the paper; attribute text as displayed in the survey language. In Japan an administrative error showed respondents drawn for 'somewhat dangerous' or 'very dangerous' both descriptors in one level (stored as displayed; public safety has 3 levels).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two hypothetical countries (A/B) the respondent would prefer to be born and grow up in (forced, no opt-out); rating = how happy the respondent would be to have been born and grown up in each country, 1 = extremely unhappy to 7 = extremely happy. Levels independently randomized with equal probability; attribute order randomized per respondent (only the position of the democracy block is recorded). N = 1,037 as in the paper; attribute text as displayed in the survey language.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two hypothetical countries (A/B) the respondent would prefer to be born and grow up in (forced, no opt-out); rating = how happy the respondent would be to have been born and grown up in each country, 1 = extremely unhappy to 7 = extremely happy. Levels independently randomized with equal probability; attribute order randomized per respondent (only the position of the democracy block is recorded). N = 1,024 as in the paper; attribute text as displayed in the survey language.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two ads is more political ('Which of these two ads is more political?', pilot wording), forced choice, no opt-out. Ads were images; attribute values are the authors' labels (sponsor, message short label, image), not the ad text. 96 tasks without an answer omitted; task order as display order not documented.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating = interest in running for the described city-council seat, 1 'No interest whatsoever' to 10 'Highest possible interest' (question wording not deposited); single-profile text vignette, 8 per respondent. Sentence order randomized once per respondent (attrpos_); level probabilities not stated. N = 3,000 as in the paper's Table 1; YouGov weight kept.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = in which of two side-by-side scenarios (A/B) Petro would be more likely to pay the doctor a bribe (forced, no opt-out); rating = how likely Petro would be to pay a bribe to get treatment more quickly, rating_self = how likely the respondent would be in Petro's position, both 1 = definitely no to 7 = definitely yes (mapped from Russian answer text; higher = more likely to bribe). Attribute levels are stored as displayed in Ukrainian or Russian, so each level has two spellings and cross-language level pairs never co-occur. Tasks without a forced-choice answer dropped; 3,037 of the 3,060 analysed respondents have this scenario, matching the authors' long file.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = in which of two side-by-side scenarios (A/B) Nina would be more likely to pay the instructor a bribe (forced, no opt-out); rating = how likely Nina would be to pay a bribe to get the license more quickly, rating_self = how likely the respondent would be in Nina's position, both 1 = definitely no to 7 = definitely yes (mapped from Russian answer text; higher = more likely to bribe). Attribute levels are stored as displayed in Ukrainian or Russian, so each level has two spellings and cross-language level pairs never co-occur. Tasks without a forced-choice answer dropped; 3,031 of the 3,060 analysed respondents have this scenario, matching the authors' long file.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One candidate per task, no choice: rating_conservative = guess of the candidate's ideology (1 Conservative, 0 Liberal), rating_sure = sureness (1-4 from answer text), rating_favorability = 0-10 (wording not in the deposit). Same respondents as the JAH module of goggin_2020_party_guess; 177 of 1,000 have no ideology profiles saved and are dropped (823 kept). Task order inferred from row order.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One candidate per task, no choice: rating_republican = guess of the candidate's party (1 Republican, 0 Democrat), rating_sure = sureness (1 very unsure to 4 very sure, coded from the answer text), rating_favorability = 0 very unfavorable to 10 very favorable (wording not in the deposit). The three issue priorities are drawn without replacement. Two CCES team modules pooled (cov_cces_module); 2,000 respondents.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which of the two scenarios do you prefer?' (Citizen Forum A/B; translated), forced, no opt-out; rating = 'In your view, how do you feel about Citizen Forum A/B?' 1 = I don't like it at all to 7 = I like it very much (translated). Attributes fully randomized; attribute order randomized per respondent with the issue always first (not recorded). Levels are the authors' English labels of German text; no survey weight deposited although the article reports a weighted sample.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which of these two immigrant profiles would you select for admission to the United States?', one forced-choice task per respondent, no opt-out. The two profiles of a pair share each context value (different signals, e.g. Poland/Germany) and always differ in education; contexts were assigned by an adaptive bandit, then arms 7 and 10 were re-fielded as validation phases (trial_phase). Left/right position is inferred from the recorded choice; cov_garbage is the authors' exclusion flag, and 121 repeat submissions by the same Prolific IDs are dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcomes: forced choice of the preferred of two COVID-19 policy proposals (no opt-out), a 0-10 support rating of each ('definitiv dagegen'-'definitiv dafuer'), 0-10 trust in government asked about one randomly drawn proposal per task, and 0-10 vaccination likelihood asked only of unvaccinated respondents (wording paraphrased). The two proposals of a task always differ and share the severity scenario; trust is NA for 141 respondents with a programming-error flag; policy levels are short German design labels.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which candidate the participant would vote for for President (forced choice among 2 or 3 candidates, no opt-out). Six within-subject blocks (trial_block: 5/8/11 attributes x 2/3 candidates; trial_block_iter = order); attributes left out of a block are '(not shown)', attribute rows randomized per subject-block (attrpos_). Race, military service and religion levels have unequal design weights. 122 participants as in the article; 11 trials without eye-tracking data flagged trial_fixation_data = 0.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One statement per task, no choice: rating = 'Would you consider this an election pledge?' 1 = yes, 0 = no; rating_accountable = should the sender be held accountable (1 yes / 0 no); rating_priority, rating_can_act, rating_cannot_check on 1-5 scales (higher = more agreement / more able). 'Don't know' is NA. Statements without a numeric goal, time horizon or condition store '(not shown)' for that clause. The deposit has 1,800 in the deposit (appendix C1: 2,031); the paper does not say what removed the difference.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One statement per task, no choice: rating = 'Would you consider this an election pledge?' 1 = yes, 0 = no; rating_accountable = should the sender be held accountable (1 yes / 0 no); rating_priority, rating_can_act, rating_cannot_check on 1-5 scales (higher = more agreement / more able). 'Don't know' is NA. Statements without a numeric goal, time horizon or condition store '(not shown)' for that clause. The deposit has 2,050 in the deposit (appendix C1: 2,214); the paper does not say what removed the difference.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One statement per task, no choice: rating = 'Would you consider this an election pledge?' 1 = yes, 0 = no; rating_accountable = should the sender be held accountable (1 yes / 0 no); rating_priority, rating_can_act, rating_cannot_check on 1-5 scales (higher = more agreement / more able). 'Don't know' is NA. Statements without a numeric goal, time horizon or condition store '(not shown)' for that clause. The deposit has 1,745 in the deposit (appendix C1: 2,032); the paper does not say what removed the difference.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two candidates the respondent would vote for (paraphrase; wording not in the deposit), forced choice, no opt-out, 10 tasks. Sample restricted by the author to single-race White, Black, Asian and Hispanic respondents (cov_race); 6 tasks without an answer are omitted. Covariate labels from the author's do-file.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which candidate the respondent would vote for (authors' 'Electoral Choice'; question wording not deposited), with a third, undocumented response coded 3 in 257 of 2,510 tasks treated as an opt-out (both profiles 0). Restriction: every pair shows one incumbent mayor and one candidate without mayoral experience. Attribute text is the appendix's English version. N = 502 as in the paper.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two policy packages the respondent preferred (forced choice; wording not in the deposit). Five three-level attributes (mortgage and credit-card interest rates, social assistance, unemployment insurance, income tax), every level pair present. Profile number is not screen position (the deposit has no position column and its rows are shuffled). N = 1,286 as in the codebook.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "If you had to choose between them, which candidate do you prefer?" (forced, no opt-out); rating = approval of each candidate, 1 = strongly disapprove to 7 = strongly approve. Six countries pooled (cov_country); attribute text is the English instrument with [COUNTRY] in the migration levels, since the national-language labels in the deposit are truncated. Levels randomized without restrictions; attribute order randomized once per respondent (not recorded). N = 10,347 as in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Between-subject label arm (trial_label): choice_more_right = which candidate is more to the right (right arm), choice_more_left = which is more to the left (left arm), both forced choice with no opt-out, NA on the other arm; rating = placement of each candidate on a 1-10 left-right scale (anchors not in the deposit; higher = more right in the data). Respondents over 69 dropped as by the authors (1); the authors' satisficer and fast-task exclusions (1,330 attentive respondents) are left to the user via cov_attention_pass_1/_2 and trial_page_submit_sec. Wording paraphrased from the authors' code (no questionnaire in the deposit).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Please select which country you would MOST prefer to live in' (two countries with different features to their democracy), forced choice, no opt-out, 5 tasks. 15 respondents screened out at an attention check before the conjoint are excluded (623 = article N); 6 who failed the post-conjoint check are kept with cov_attention_pass_2 = 0. Demographics are unlabelled Qualtrics codes.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two news items the respondent would choose to read (paraphrase; wording not in the deposit), forced choice, no opt-out, 12 tasks per respondent. Partisans only (cov_dem / cov_rep). Two attributes: headline text and outlet; the two items share a topic in about 9% of tasks and an outlet in about 34%, with no restriction documented. Qualtrics response ids re-keyed; the author's derived topic and friendly/unfriendly-source dummies dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two news items the respondent would choose to read (paraphrase; wording not in the deposit), forced choice, no opt-out, 10 tasks per respondent. Partisans only (cov_dem / cov_rep). Two attributes: headline text and outlet; the two items share a topic in about 9% of tasks and an outlet in about 34%, with no restriction documented. Qualtrics response ids re-keyed; the author's derived topic and friendly/unfriendly-source dummies dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One profile per task: rating = how typical the person described is of welfare recipients, 0-10 (higher = more typical; end labels not in the deposit); no choice question. Respondents saw one of two instruction versions (trial_instruction_code 1/2; wording not deposited). All 1,893 respondents with ratings are kept; the article analyses the 1,293 non-Hispanic whites. 94 respondents rated fewer than 30 profiles.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Text vignette: statements of two hypothetical politicians; choice_listen/_crooked/_immigration/_conservative = which politician is more likely to say that politicians should always listen to the people / many in the political class are crooked / immigration should be reduced / to have conservative ideology (forced, no opt-out); rating_listen/_crooked/_immigration 1 = not at all likely to 5 = extremely likely; rating_ideology 1-5 left-right (UK wording; end labels unavailable). Control levels (no people-centrism or anti-elitism statement) and the undisplayed party are '(not shown)'. Finished respondents with any answer: 690.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Text vignette: statements of two hypothetical politicians; choice_listen/_crooked/_immigration/_conservative = which politician is more likely to say that politicians should always listen to the people / many in the political class are crooked / immigration should be reduced / to have conservative ideology (forced, no opt-out); rating_listen/_crooked/_immigration 1 = not at all likely to 5 = extremely likely; rating_ideology 1-5 1 = very liberal to 5 = very conservative. Control levels (no people-centrism or anti-elitism statement) and the undisplayed party are '(not shown)'. Finished respondents with any answer: 699.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Text vignette: statements of two hypothetical politicians; choice_listen/_crooked/_immigration/_conservative = which politician is more likely to say that politicians should always listen to the people / many in the political class are crooked / immigration should be reduced / to have conservative ideology (forced, no opt-out); rating_listen/_crooked/_immigration 1 = not at all likely to 5 = extremely likely; rating_ideology 1-5 1 = very liberal to 5 = very conservative. Control levels (no people-centrism or anti-elitism statement) and the undisplayed party are '(not shown)'. Finished respondents with any answer: 704.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two same-party candidates the respondent would vote for ('Which of the two candidates would you like to vote for? Even if you are not entirely sure, please indicate which of the two you would prefer if you had to choose either one of them.', translated from Japanese), forced choice, no opt-out. All 1,152 profiles possible (no restrictions); attribute order randomized per respondent, not recorded; attribute text is the authors' English translation. N = 2,686 as in the paper.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcome: forced choice between two candidates (wording not in the deposit; paraphrase), no opt-out. Level shares are unequal and dependent: legal and farming occupations appear almost only with Abitur, and a 6-year membership dominates for candidates with legislative experience; no pair is fully absent, the scheme is undocumented, and AMCEs should condition on these pairs as the authors do. Attribute text is German (the .dta value labels); 50 respondents with no conjoint answers dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating = 'On a scale from strongly oppose to strongly support, where would you place your level of support for this potential nominee?' 1-5 (strongly oppose to strongly support); rating_trust = trust in the nominee's impartiality, 1-5 (wording not deposited). Single-profile ratings, task order inferred from row order; trial_rhetoric is a respondent-level arm (elite rhetoric shown or not). Attribute levels come from the authors' code; the 'Think-tank' level is labelled 'Chief counsel' in their figures. The authors' additive legitimacy index is not included; 7 rows with no outcome dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two candidates the respondent would vote for (wording not in the deposit; one chosen per task, no opt-out observed). Attribute text is the deposit's English labels for a Spanish-language survey; 'No Opinion'/'No Information'/'No Favorite...' are stored as levels, though whether they were displayed as text is undocumented. The codebook's 0 = voted for is contradicted by the data and analysis (1 = chosen used). The deposited day counts past ages 18/70 (which fix the date of birth, the RD running variable) are dropped; cov_age keeps completed years. N = 2,042.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcome: forced choice of which of two dating profiles to select (wording not in the deposit), no opt-out. A fixed D-optimal design of 16 pairs shown to everyone in random order (order not recorded; task is the set number); race and attractiveness were conveyed by profile photos. Profile gender is set by respondent orientation, not randomized; IP, location, Prolific IDs and free text dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two candidates the respondent selected (paraphrase), forced choice, no opt-out; rating = 0-10 evaluation of each candidate (0 very negative, 10 very positive), present for chosen and non-chosen profiles although the codebook says the chosen one was rated. Task and profile are inferred from row order. Attribute levels are the codebook's descriptions.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating = support for the proposed policy on 1-7 (higher = more support; wording not deposited, paraphrased from the author's do-file); choice = forced choice between the two proposals, no opt-out. Within a task the two profiles never share a coercion level; the policy goal is fixed per task (trial_goal). Attribute levels are the author's English value labels, the Hebrew display text is not deposited. 69 respondents flagged as low quality by the author (dropped in her analyses) are kept with cov_low_quality = 1.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating = support for the proposed policy on 1-7 (higher = more support; wording not deposited, paraphrased from the author's do-file); choice = forced choice between the two proposals, no opt-out. Within a task the two profiles never share a coercion level; the policy goal is fixed per task (trial_goal). Attribute levels are the author's English value labels. 200 respondents flagged as low quality by the author (dropped in her analyses) are kept with cov_low_quality = 1.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Who would you personally trust more as an authority on religious matters?' and choice_listen = 'If you could only listen to a sermon by one of these preachers, which one would you choose to listen to?', both forced choice without opt-out; rating = trust in each preacher, stored 0-4 (Not trust at all to Completely trust) as the authors code it. Nationality 'home country' was piped per respondent, so Saudi respondents never see the foreign 'Saudi Arabia' level. All 14,466 respondents kept; the paper's N of 12,025 is the Sunni and Salafi subset (cov_sect).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One immigrant profile per task; respondents guessed the immigrant's world region (Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America or the Middle East). The single five-option answer is stored as rating_africa .. rating_middle_east, 1 = that region was chosen (exactly one per row). No choice among profiles. Benefits and police record are 'none' with probability 1/2, otherwise one of several specific labels; other attributes uniform and independent. N = 1,979 as in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single neighbour vignette; ratings kept raw: rating = 'Say you had loaned this neighbor some money, would you trust them to pay it back?' (1 No, 2 Yes), rating_donations / rating_follow_headman / rating_share_well 1 Very likely to 4 Not at all likely (higher = less likely), rating_way_of_life 1 Agree / 2 Disagree; don't know and refusals NA. Only the non-co-ethnic arm (6,209 of 12,362) is kept because the deposit did not save the ethnic group shown to the 6,153 co-ethnic-arm respondents, so the co-ethnic contrast cannot be estimated (the arm was randomized, so the rest is a random subset); the title text's pronoun follows the neighbour's gender; 21 respondents with no answer omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two persons is more of a Democrat (Democrat arm) or Republican (Republican arm), forced, no opt-out; rating: 7-point partisanship rating of each person, kept raw (anchors not in the deposit; the authors' code implies 1 = Democrat end, 7 = Republican end in both arms). Wording paraphrased (Online Appendix A not deposited). Attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). All 1,051 respondents kept with trial_page_seconds and two attention-check covariates; the authors analyse 864 attentive respondents.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice of which of two applicants should be given priority in admission to the Naval Academy (wording paraphrased; not in the deposit), no opt-out. Level text as recorded by the survey; the appendix's race level 'Other' never occurs; gender Non-binary appears on about 10% of profiles. One task with no recorded choice and two free-text items dropped. 582 respondents, as in the paper.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which candidate do you think should be given priority in faculty recruitment?", forced choice between two candidates, no opt-out. Level text as recorded; department has 9 levels in the data although the appendix lists 4, race 'Other' never occurs, gender Non-binary appears on about 10% of profiles. Two free-text items dropped. 572 respondents, as in the paper.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two politicians the respondent prefers as a national security defender (paraphrase; questionnaire not deposited); an opt-out is inferred from the data (both profiles never chosen; 5,105 of 11,225 tasks with neither chosen, choice = 0 on both). Attribute levels are the deposit's English value labels; respondents saw Traditional Chinese. Covariates are the authors' coarsened versions (born before 1978, college, residence in the 6 capitals, perceived relations).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment: choice between a gasoline car (profile 1, fixed price 0.85 x budget, 2 per 100 miles, 400 miles; charging rows not shown) and an electric version (profile 2), forced, no opt-out; question wording paraphrased. Attribute text rebuilt from the deposit's numbers with the templates of the authors' screenshot; the text of 0-minute, 60-minute and not-available levels is unverified. Task order is row order (display order not recorded). New- and used-car arms in trial_car_type. Home ZIP codes dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two hypothetical candidates the respondent prefers as vice-presidential nominee (paraphrase; no questionnaire deposited), forced, no opt-out. Task 2 is the same fixed pair for every respondent (trial_fixed_pair = 1), which makes pooled level shares unequal; tasks 1, 3-5 are fully randomized. 16 of 599 respondents lack 1-3 tasks. Covariates keep the source codes. Prolific IDs and per-task follow-up items with no recorded wording dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment: choice between Reward A and Reward B ("which of the two rewards would motivate you more in a family-based weight management program"; wording varies slightly by task), forced, no opt-out. Fixed blocked fractional-factorial design (30 versions of 10 tasks, trial_version). The payment-structure text named the profile's own value; it is stored with the placeholder [total value]. cov_survey_weight is the sampling weight. Deposit has 305 respondents, article 304.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcomes: forced choice "Which policy do you prefer?" and "How much do you support or oppose <Policy>?" rated 1-5 (5 = strongly support, direction from the authors' recode; no value labels deposited). No opt-out. trial_frame is the randomized framing arm shown before the conjoint. The article says 149 attention-check failures were removed from 1,180, but the deposit holds all 1,180 and the authors' models use them. Qualtrics IDs re-keyed; ambiguous cost-of-living binaries dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcome: forced choice between two parties/candidates described by six policy proposals (wording not deposited; paraphrased from the authors' code), exactly one chosen per task, no opt-out. One of four country tables from the same study; the domestic-policy text is specific to the host country. Respondents saw English or Traditional Chinese; only English level text is deposited. Qualtrics IDs re-keyed; the authors' derived bins dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcome: forced choice between two parties/candidates described by six policy proposals (wording not deposited; paraphrased from the authors' code), exactly one chosen per task, no opt-out. Qualtrics IDs re-keyed; the authors' derived bins dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcome: choice of which of two products to buy (wording not deposited; paraphrase), exactly one per round, no opt-out. Each respondent saw one randomly assigned product type (trial_product_type), and price and functional-duration levels are specific to that product. Level text is the authors' English recode of German labels. The authors' survey weight and attribute-order variables are not deposited; respondents with any missing conjoint answer were dropped before deposit.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcome: "Which of these two flights would you choose?" (Flight 1 / Flight 2), forced, no opt-out. Attribute order randomized per respondent and recorded (attrpos_). cov_survey_weight is the deposit's weight. The fuel-type level text keeps the source's spelling 'Sutainable'. ZIP codes and Qualtrics IDs dropped, as were the omnibus survey's unrelated items.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment: "Which system would you prefer (Please choose only one option)?" among AI-DSS 1-3 or "None of these"; the opt-out is not a profile, so choice is 0 on all three profiles in 995 of 3,823 tasks. Fixed design of 5 choice sets shown to everyone, with collinear levels; task is the choice-set number, not the order shown (randomized, not recorded). 20 respondents answered fewer than 5 sets. Platform IDs re-keyed; free-text specialization dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single vignette per respondent (task = profile = 1). choice: "Would you be likely to comply with the instructions from {Authority}?" Yes = 1 / No = 0 (accept/reject, so opt_out = yes). Ratings: others' compliance 1 None .. 4 Most; whether the authority has the right to ask, whether the action lowers one's risk, whether the authority would monitor (1 Yes, 0 No). Don't know/refuse -> NA. The religious-leader authority arm (1,510 respondents) is excluded because the piped level text was not saved; 6 respondents with no outcome answer omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Ratings of perceived anti-elitism and people-centrism of each candidate, 1-6 (codebook anchors). No choice question. Arms: party affiliation shown or not ('(not shown)'). Level frequencies follow the 2017 HoR candidate distribution (nonuniform). Wording from the deposit's English codebook (Japanese survey).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Rating of each candidate's desirability as a member of the House of Representatives, 1-6. No choice question. Manipulated-mediator arm adds a 'special note' per candidate (4 notes, each used once per respondent); in the natural-mediator arm the note is '(not shown)'. Wording from the deposit's English codebook (Japanese survey).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Pilot 1 for Study 2: ratings of perceived anti-elitism and people-centrism of each candidate, 1-6. No choice question. Manipulated-mediator arm adds a 'special note' per candidate (8 notes, each used once per respondent; note set differs between pilots); natural-mediator arm '(not shown)'. Wording from the deposit's English codebook (Japanese survey).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Pilot 2 for Study 2: ratings of perceived anti-elitism and people-centrism of each candidate, 1-6. No choice question. Manipulated-mediator arm adds a 'special note' per candidate (8 notes, each used once per respondent; note set differs between pilots); natural-mediator arm '(not shown)'. Wording from the deposit's English codebook (Japanese survey).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Pilot 3 for Study 2: ratings of perceived anti-elitism and people-centrism of each candidate, 1-6. No choice question. Manipulated-mediator arm adds a 'special note' per candidate (8 notes, each used once per respondent; note set differs between pilots); natural-mediator arm '(not shown)'. Wording from the deposit's English codebook (Japanese survey).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette experiment: 6 vignettes per respondent, one per pledge, each rated 0-10 (how acceptable the non-fulfillment of the promise is, 0 = not at all acceptable, 10 = fully acceptable). Level text is the English codebook labels. 2,466 in the file (paper code 2466); 44 never reached the vignettes and 55 more gave no rating, so 2,367 remain; the paper's figures keep Finnish citizens only (cov_citizenship).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette experiment: 6 vignettes per respondent, one per pledge, each rated 0-10 (how acceptable the non-fulfillment of the promise is, 0 = not at all acceptable, 10 = fully acceptable). Level text is the English codebook labels. All 1,359 respondents (paper code 1359).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette experiment: 6 vignettes per respondent, one per pledge, each rated 0-10 (propensity to vote for the pledging party, 0 = very unlikely, 10 = very likely). Level text is the English codebook labels. 4,721 rows in the file; 2,093 respondents with vignettes and ratings remain; attention test kept as cov_attention_pass.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice of the journal the respondent would submit to, between two hypothetical journals (3 tasks); exact wording not deposited, no opt-out. Attribute levels are the deposit's short English labels; covariates are Spanish answer text named by question number. 4 unanswered tasks dropped, leaving 445 of the paper's 446 respondents; Qualtrics IDs and one free-text field dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two hypothetical politicians (no opt-out); question wording not deposited. Attribute levels are issue statements in the survey language. Sample as prepared by the authors (quota sample with attention check plus Eastern German oversample); one of three samples from the same study, each its own table.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two hypothetical politicians (no opt-out); question wording not deposited. Attribute levels are issue statements in the survey language. Sample as prepared by the authors; one of three samples from the same study, each its own table.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two hypothetical politicians (no opt-out); question wording not deposited. Attribute levels are issue statements in the survey language. Sample as prepared by the authors; one of three samples from the same study, each its own table.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two property tax policies (no opt-out) and a 1-5 rating of each (variable rank; wording and anchors not deposited). Level text is the deposit's terse English value labels. SSI and Qualtrics panels pooled as in the authors' combined model (trial_panel); 5 respondents have fewer than 4 tasks.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Lab-in-the-field conjoint: forced choice between two property tax policies (no opt-out) and a 1-5 rating of each (variable rank; wording and anchors not deposited). Level text is the deposit's terse English value labels. Separate design from the online conjoint (six attributes).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two coal phase-out scenarios (no opt-out) and a 1-7 rating of each (1 = very poor, 7 = very good); exact wording not deposited. Fixed blocked design (500 versions); attribute text is the article's English Table 1. The paper excludes attention-check failures (N = 1984); all 2161 are kept with cov_attention_pass. Cost framing (household only vs household plus economy-wide) is in trial_conjoint_type with undocumented codes; postcode and place of residence dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two coal phase-out scenarios (no opt-out) and a 1-7 rating of each (1 = very poor, 7 = very good); exact wording not deposited. Fixed blocked design (500 versions); attribute text is the article's English Table 1. The paper excludes attention-check failures (N = 491); all 533 are kept with cov_attention_pass. Cost framing (household only vs household plus economy-wide) is in trial_conjoint_type with undocumented codes; postcode and place of residence dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two coal phase-out scenarios (no opt-out) and a 1-7 rating of each (1 = very poor, 7 = very good); exact wording not deposited. Fixed blocked design (500 versions); attribute text is the article's English Table 1. The paper excludes attention-check failures (N = 473); all 501 are kept with cov_attention_pass. Cost framing (household only vs household plus economy-wide) is in trial_conjoint_type with undocumented codes; postcode and place of residence dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice is the official's pick of which of two collaborative programs to adopt (wording not deposited; paraphrase), forced choice, no opt-out. Attribute levels are the author's short labels (e.g. 750:250, Republicans), not the displayed wording. 43 of 772 officials answered fewer than 3 pairs (missing pairs absent, task numbers kept). City identifiers and city census figures dropped; party, gender, education and tenure kept as undocumented codes (_code).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which of these two candidates would you be most likely to vote for?" between candidates of two parties with the displayed policy packages; forced choice, no opt-out. Levels drawn uniformly and independently; attribute order randomized per respondent (not recorded); profile position inferred from row order. Unanswered tasks and one respondent ID holding two complete sessions dropped: 1,403 respondents against 1,394 in the paper. Platform IDs re-keyed; party ID, education and nation kept as undocumented codes.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette (one per respondent): three 1-10 ratings of the described MP's competence, whether a pawn of party elites, and cooperativeness (pre-registered wording; endpoint labels undocumented; higher = more of the named trait). The politician factor has 3 arms by design (man / woman district-elected, woman quota-elected; no quota man) with probabilities 25/25/50. Don't know/refused are NA; 13 respondents with no rating dropped (914 of 927). cov_manip_correct is the post-vignette quota manipulation check (9 = don't know/refused).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating is a 0-100 feeling thermometer for each stranger; choice is which of the two the respondent would prefer to talk to (forced, no opt-out); wording paraphrased from the article (Czech wording not deposited). Unrestricted design, attribute order fixed. 321 tasks with unsaved attribute text and 14 with no answer dropped; 1,032 respondents and 10,250 rows as in the article. Qualtrics IDs re-keyed; attribute and covariate text in Czech.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Two-stage design with one task of nine aspirant profiles: rating_deselected = ticked under "Wen würden Sie nicht nominieren?" (exactly three of nine; 1 = deselected), rating_list_position = list position 1-6 assigned to each kept profile in stage 2 (1 = top; NA for deselected). Each respondent saw only one of the two dual-candidacy attributes (regional vs state/federal list); the other is (not shown). Attribute order randomized per respondent and recorded. Qualtrics metadata, free text and the years respondents joined their party or executive dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two applicants should be hired (forced, no opt-out). Each respondent did a private-company set and a public-school set (trial_job), in random order that is not recorded; both sets show the same 7 applicant pairs (trial_pair), and the first pair of each set is repeated at its end (trial_repeat_of, profiles not swapped). Names never repeat within a pair. Attribute text is Japanese as displayed; names carry ethnicity and gender (see crosswalk). Platform IDs and free-text answers dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two applicants should be hired (forced, no opt-out). Each respondent did a private-company set and a public-school set (trial_job), in random order that is not recorded; both sets show the same 7 applicant pairs (trial_pair), and the first pair of each set is repeated at its end (trial_repeat_of, profiles not swapped). Names never repeat within a pair. Attribute text is Japanese as displayed; names carry ethnicity and gender (see crosswalk). Platform IDs and free-text answers dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single-profile ratings: rating_support ("Do you support the use of AI under these circumstances?") and rating_trust ("Do you trust the use of AI under these circumstances?"), both 1-5 (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree); no choice, no opt-out. Five tasks per respondent in the data although the article says four. Platform IDs, ZIP code, unlabelled Lucid profile codes and the separate follow-up mediation experiment dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette survey: each MP read one German-language negotiation vignette (2x2: decision pressure x election-campaign proximity); attribute text is the codebook's English description, not the vignette prose. 23 rating_ outcomes on 1-5 scales (likelihood of publicizing via 10 channel/content combinations, of agreeing on confidentiality, of compromising; vignette realism; two manipulation checks whose anchors differ, see conj_outcomes). No choice, no opt-out; one row per respondent, id is the row number.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One pair of hypothetical National Assembly candidates per respondent; choice = "Which candidate would you vote for?" (forced; 1,147 don't-know/refusals omitted). Attribute text is the file's value labels, Vietnamese for gender and province and English for the rest; the candidate's province is by design the respondent's own or Hanoi. cov_survey_weight is the PAPI sampling weight used in the authors' svyset (which also post-stratifies by province population, cov_province_population). Village and commune identifiers and free text dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Which policy do you prefer?" (forced, no opt-out); rating = likelihood of voting for each proposal in a referendum, 1 = definitely against to 10 = definitely in favor. Fully randomized, attribute order randomized per respondent (not recorded). Respondents have 1-4 tasks (N matches the article). cov_party_id is missing for respondents who named no party; cov_survey_weight is the authors' entropy-balancing weight. Derived dummies and groupings dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Pilot study with income changes in percent. choice = preferred policy of each pair (forced, no opt-out; the pilot's wording is not deposited, the main study asked "Which policy do you prefer?"). Task and profile are inferred from row order (the file has neither). No rating or covariates in the deposit.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Validation study: choice = preferred proposal (or candidate) of each pair, forced, no opt-out; wording of this instrument not deposited. trial_version is the randomly assigned framing (generic policy, health care policy, trade policy, candidate platform), constant within respondent. Profile position is inferred from row order within each recorded task. 2,003 of the 2,300 fielded respondents are in the file (matches the article's analysis N).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcome: forced choice of which of two hypothetical parties' candidate (district vote, trial_context (S/M)MD) or party (PR vote) is preferable; skipping was allowed and the 524 skipped tasks (2.8%) are omitted, so 1,834 of 1,866 respondents remain. Tasks 1-5 are always the district block although block order was randomized for half the sample (not recorded), so task is not the display order across blocks. Levels are the authors' English labels; randomization was restricted to realistic combinations (e.g. MPs vs ministers, committee chairs, bills), so level shares are unequal. Attribute order was randomized per respondent and is kept as attrpos_*.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcomes: forced choice between two immigrants (the authors' 'supporting admission'; question wording not deposited) and rating_entry, a per-profile entry decision stored in Korean and coded here 1 = entry banned, 2 = entry allowed with a mandatory 14-day quarantine, 3 = entry allowed. Profile position was not recorded, so profile numbers are arbitrary within a task. Attribute levels are the authors' English labels, including their typos ('volumne', 'communitation'). Randomization restrictions and attribute order are undocumented.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcomes: forced choice between two trade agreements and a 1-7 rating of each (1 'muy en contra' .. 7 'muy a favor'); no opt-out. Payoff levels are an English rendering of the article's example (euro); randomization excluded agreements with losses on all three payoffs and pairs identical on the payoffs. 2,999 respondents (article: 3,000; one respondent has no conjoint rows). The authors pooled this sample with the Polish one (dur_2025_trade_poland).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcomes: forced choice between two trade agreements and a 1-7 rating of each (1 'muy en contra' .. 7 'muy a favor'); no opt-out. Payoff levels are an English rendering of the article's example (zloty, 5 x the euro value); randomization excluded agreements with losses on all three payoffs and pairs identical on the payoffs. 2,999 respondents (article: 3,000; one respondent has no conjoint rows). The authors pooled this sample with the Spanish one (dur_2025_trade_spain).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcomes: forced choice between two trade agreements and a 1-7 rating of each (1 'strongly oppose' .. 7 'strongly favour'); no opt-out. Pairs identical on the two payoff attributes were redrawn; attribute order randomized (payoffs kept together) but not recorded. N = 2,128 matches the article, and its Table 4 reproduces exactly.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcomes: forced choice of the more appealing of two vaccination-call scenarios and a 0-10 rating of the likelihood of heeding each (0 'would definitely not get vaccinated' .. 10 'would definitely get vaccinated'); no opt-out. Austria and Italy pooled (cov_country), level text is the English version of the German and Italian instruments. The testimonial was shown as a first name and age that were not saved; only its gender and same/different age group are stored. Levels drawn with equal probability from the full factorial.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcomes: forced choice of the media report that makes vaccination more trustworthy and a 0-10 rating of the likelihood of getting vaccinated given each report (0 'would definitely not get vaccinated' .. 10 'would definitely get vaccinated'); no opt-out. Austria and Italy pooled (cov_country); level text is the English version of the German and Italian instruments. Levels drawn with equal probability from the full factorial.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcomes: choice of one of two hypothetical persons (question wording not deposited; the authors treat it as which should have voting rights) and a 1-7 rating of each (the authors code 5-7 as granting and 1-3 as denying the vote; anchors not deposited). 22-43 respondents per pair skipped the choice (choice NA on both profiles, ratings kept); 29 profile ratings are missing. Level text is the authors' value labels. The 19 respondents Qualtrics did not flag as good completers are dropped, as in the authors' analysis (N = 980).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcome: forced choice of which of two candidates the respondent would prefer as president of Chile; 2,245 of 9,000 tasks have no recorded choice and are omitted, so 1,542 of 1,800 respondents remain. Level text is the deposit's Spanish value labels, four of which Stata had truncated at 60 characters and are completed here; the article's attribute table words several levels differently, so the exact displayed wording is uncertain. cov_survey_weight is the survey weight the author uses in every model.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette survey, one vignette per task. rating: how likely the vet in the scenario is to prescribe without visiting the farm, circled -5 (definitely would not) to +5 (definitely would), stored by the authors as 1-11; rating_others: proportion of vets who would prescribe, grouped to 10% bands and coded 1-10. Vignettes drawn from 384 combinations by a resolution-V D-efficient design; factor order fixed. Level text is the clause printed in the example survey. 10 vignettes with neither outcome omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two persons stands higher in Swiss society today (forced, no opt-out); rating: each person's position on the 1 (unten) to 10 (oben) status ladder; wording German. Choice and rating files have different respondent numbering and were joined by each respondent's unique set of 10 profiles (2,319 matched; 63 respondents have choice only, 117 rating only, these without covariates). Attribute text is the authors' English labels; occupation and education combine only in fixed ways (observed restriction).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: one of three T-shirts per task (question wording not deposited; exactly one chosen in every task, no opt-out recorded). Attribute levels are the .dta value labels; price shown as 5/10/15/20 (display format unknown). Restrictions and attribute order undocumented. MTurk IDs, ZIP codes and derived dummies dropped; 44 respondents lack wave-1 covariates.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: one of three televisions per task (question wording not deposited; exactly one chosen in every task, no opt-out recorded). Attribute levels as stored text; price as value labels such as 1,00,000. Restrictions, attribute order and survey language undocumented. Worker-ID column, free-text city and occupation, and derived dummies dropped; birth year kept as recorded, with implausible values.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of Construction Plan A and B the respondent would accept (forced, no opt-out); rating: willingness to accept each plan, 1 (absolutely not willing) to 7 (very strongly willing); wording and levels are the codebook's English translation of a Japanese survey. Attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_*); no documented restrictions. Municipality of residence dropped; one implausible age (3) set to NA, 13 respondents aged 14-17 kept.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two candidates the respondent would prefer as the leading candidate for their party in the upcoming parliamentary election (article's English; forced, no opt-out). Half the respondents first read that the terrorist threat to Denmark is significant (trial_terror_threat = Yes). Origin and education levels were weighted to match Danish candidates (Danmark ~79% of profiles). Source respondent IDs re-keyed.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice between two policy packages (wording not published); rating: support for each package, 1 (strongly opposed) to 7 (strongly support). Countries pooled (cov_country). Attribute text is the authors' English labels; the car-requirement levels are stored in miles per gallon for all three countries, though the article lists l/100 km for the non-US versions. 'No tax revenues' appears only with 'No new tax'. Attribute order randomized per respondent but not recorded.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two news stories per task (the authors' `chosen`), no opt-out; question wording not in the deposit. Headline is the authors' short label, not the displayed wording; photo levels describe photographs. Qualtrics Conjoint with 260 design versions (trial_design_version); restrictions and level probabilities undocumented. Respondents can recur across the four darr_2026 tables but IDs are not linkable.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two news stories per task (the authors' `chosen`), no opt-out; question wording not in the deposit. Headline and note are the authors' value labels (headline stored as codes GC1/GC2/GC bad 1/GC bad 2), not the displayed wording; photo levels describe photographs. Qualtrics Conjoint with 260 design versions (trial_design_version); restrictions and level probabilities undocumented. Respondents can recur across the four darr_2026 tables but IDs are not linkable.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two news stories per task (the authors' `chosen`), no opt-out; question wording not in the deposit. The respondent's state piped into the headline is stored as [your state]; photo levels describe photographs. Qualtrics Conjoint with 260 design versions (trial_design_version); restrictions and level probabilities undocumented. Respondents can recur across the four darr_2026 tables but IDs are not linkable.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two news stories per task (the authors' `chosen`), no opt-out; question wording not in the deposit. Headline, note and pledge are the authors' short labels, not the displayed wording; 39 tasks of 7 respondents who left early are dropped; photo levels describe photographs. Qualtrics Conjoint with 260 design versions (trial_design_version); restrictions and level probabilities undocumented. Respondents can recur across the four darr_2026 tables but IDs are not linkable.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two policy profiles per task (`selected`), no opt-out; question wording not in the deposit. Levels are the authors' English labels; the display language is not documented. Observed restriction: Medical Aid never shown with Palestinian illness Deterioration and Monitor never with Improvement, so those levels are rarer. 334 unanswered tasks dropped (1,586 of 1,589 respondents remain).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Four forced choices per pair of e-bike policy packages, no opt-out: choice = preferred standard, choice_increase_use = more likely to increase e-bike use, choice_more_restrictive = more restrictive for the individual, choice_more_intervention = requires more government intervention (the authors' labels; question wording not in the deposit). Levels in English; display language not documented. cov_survey_weight kept.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Which deal are you more likely to choose?" and choice_wrong = "Which deal is more likely to go wrong?", each with Both and Neither options: those answers are 0 on both profiles, raw answer in trial_choice_response / trial_wrong_response (the authors count Both as chosen). rating = trust in the deal, 0-10 slider. Levels are the authors' English labels; party is stored even for Businessman owners, display undocumented. Bank account rounds 1-2, TV rounds 3-4 (trial_product). 696 unanswered tasks and never-reached respondents dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Wenn Sie sich für eines der beiden Autos entscheiden müssten, welches Auto würden Sie kaufen?" (forced, no opt-out); rating: "Würden Sie Auto A/B kaufen?" Ja = 1, Nein = 0. Levels independently randomized; German text as stored. trial_group records the source's two survey versions (Conjoint Pos / Neg), whose difference is not documented.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two party manifestos (`selected`), no opt-out; question wording not in the deposit (authors: vote intention). Tasks 1-5 social democratic, 6-10 liberal manifestos (trial_manifesto). Levels uniform and unconstrained; attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). The deposited manifesto ratings are not included: their scale and direction are undocumented. N = 2,119 vs 2,082 stated in the deposit.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two hypothetical people the respondent picked in the job-training conjoint (question wording not deposited; paraphrase), forced choice with exactly one chosen per task, no opt-out. Attribute levels are the authors' English translations; the authors standardized Age to 25/35/46/62. Record is unequally distributed (None about 70%). 1,882 respondents, matching the README. Year of birth kept as recorded (3 respondents born after 2005); the authors' main sample (Western, ethnic Germans) is a subset.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two hypothetical people the respondent picked in the job-training conjoint (question wording not deposited; paraphrase), forced choice with exactly one chosen per task, no opt-out. Attribute levels are the authors' English translations; the authors standardized Age to 25/35/46/62. Record is unequally distributed (None about 70%). 1,768 respondents, matching the README. Year of birth kept as recorded (12 respondents born after 2005).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette, 2 per respondent (task 1-2, profile 1). Outcomes: "how do you think he/she/they tried to resolve this problem?" and "how do you think people should resolve this issue?", each with 3 options (state authority / a religious cleric (.dta label: a local imam) / by mediation according to tradition and Kanun), stored as 0/1 indicators per option (rating_tried_*, rating_should_*). Levels are the English questionnaire wording parsed from the stored Albanian text; resources and community wording depends on the dispute and each respondent heard one civil and one criminal dispute. Per-dispute Ns and Table A1 coefficients reproduce.

Gender and caste were each signalled by a name plus a category word; the table stores the category words. 2 respondents with no condition and 6 with no outcome dropped; N 2,360 vs 2,347 in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Paired choice between two trade agreements (Agreement A, Agreement B or Neither; Neither = opt-out, 411 tasks) and a rating of each agreement 1 (not favourably at all) to 10 (very favourably); wording paraphrased from the article. Respondents are interest groups, not individuals. 5 tasks with no answer omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Choice-based conjoint: 'Please choose the protein source that you think is more sustainable on the basis of the information at your disposal' (English translation), two cards plus a 'no choice' option (opt-out; both cards 0). Fixed orthogonal design, the same 16 pairs for everyone; nutritional score, ecological score and price were each shown or not ((not shown)), with shown values fixed by product. Task order as displayed is not documented. All 639 respondents kept; the article excludes 98 (under 18 or diet due to disease) to reach 541.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment, real and incentivized: 'choose which of the two seeds you would purchase if you were at the market to buy seed. If you wouldn't buy either then choose ninguna' (enumerator script); ninguna = opt-out (both 0). Seed shown only as the plot symbol (circle = certified, square = QDS, triangle = recycled, blind to farmers). Fixed 12-pair design in four display orders. 2 farmers without a choice set and 2 invalid answers dropped. Price barely affects choice.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Incentivized referendum DCE: 'Which option do you vote for?' with a fixed 'No project' option (opt-out, all profiles 0). Three randomized formats in trial_mechanism: single binary (one project vs none, 600), sequential binary (9 questions, 300), sequential trinary (Project A vs Project B vs none, 9 questions, 300). Projects are 9 fixed bundles (fixed design); cost $5/$8/$11/$15 random. task = display order; trial_question = question number. Prolific IDs dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two development projects ('Which project do you prefer for your municipality?'), no opt-out, 4 tasks; 36 unanswered tasks omitted. Levels are the paper's English Table 1 text mapped from the deposit's short labels. Profile position inferred from the deposit's stacked row order (which project was shown first is assumed). Attribute order randomized per respondent, not recorded. Municipality ID dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice 'Which of these two birth scenarios would you choose?' between two hospital births of a first child (sex, out-of-pocket expenses $250-$10,000, birth weight 5 lb 8 oz-8 lb 13 oz, season), 7 tasks, no opt-out; orthogonal balanced main-effects design, attribute order randomized once per respondent. All 2,005 responses kept; the article's analysis sample of 1,894 is cov_main_sample = 1 (the rest were outside the US by IP, failed a repeated question or took under 2 minutes).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single-proposal referendum vote 'Stimmen Sie diesem Vorschlag zu?' (Ja / Nein / Ich möchte nicht abstimmen): choice = Ja, choice_against = Nein, abstention 0 on both (opt-out); 6 proposals per respondent in a fixed order of rising levy, justification and differentiation randomized between respondents, levy rows depend on the justification. The codebook's vote coding (0 = yes) contradicts the authors' code and the data; 1 = yes is used. All 3,169 kept; the article drops the fastest and slowest 5% by survey time.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Text vignettes in 3 pairs (French). choice: "Which politician are you most likely to vote for?" (forced, no opt-out); rating_represents, rating_trust, rating_capable (0-10 scales) stored as code 1-11 = displayed 0 (Pas du tout) .. 10 (Oui, tout à fait). Sub-Saharan African background shown about twice as often as each other background; 182 Turkish-background profiles carry North-African first names. Religion level 'pratique l'Islam'/'pratique l'islam' differs only in capitalisation by background, as stored. Part 3a profiles dropped. N = 1,199.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Agreement 1-5 (Muy en desacuerdo ... Muy de acuerdo) with '¿Qué tan de acuerdo estaría usted con pagar más impuestos <tax> para que el gobierno pueda aumentar el gasto público <area>?' (experiment 1, Q36). One sentence per respondent with two randomized clauses (control = clause omitted, '(not shown)'); Spanish clause text from the bilingual questionnaire. Pollfish online sample, Mexico, Dec 2021-Jan 2022, n = 2,401; no weight.
